research: [spread] Line movement (WagerTalk, Oct 22): opened Philadelphia -2.5 (-108) and held for over a week, then rose to -3.5 after the Sixers' opener, briefly dipped to 3 and went back to 3.5. SBR calls the move an overreaction to the Opening Night upset of the Knicks. It's a 1-point move toward the favorite; the slate's +3.5 is the market number.

[spread] Betting splits (WagerTalk, Oct 22): Philadelphia has about 75% of spread money and 66% of tickets. The line moved with the public, so this isn't reverse movement; slight contrarian lean to Cleveland.

Philadelphia won its opener 106-100 at New York (Oct 20, an earlier game). Maxey scored 28 and Brown 19 in his debut, and the defense held NY to 37% shooting with 14 forced turnovers. But the Sixers shot 11-of-40 from three, and LeBron and Embiid combined for 9-of-28 (Predictem/WagerTalk). The win came on defense, not offense.

[angle] Nurse used a seven-man rotation in the opener with all five starters over 33 minutes (WagerTalk). On one day's rest that's a load for a 41-year-old LeBron and Embiid, who has played 96 regular-season games in three years. Leans Cleveland, though Nurse is expected to use more bench at home.

[angle] Jarrett Allen was added to Cleveland's injury report Wednesday as questionable with patellar tendinopathy; if he sits, Mobley moves to center and Embiid gets a softer night on the glass (Predictem, Oct 22). A Sportsgambler preview listed Allen in a projected starting five; status unresolved. Uncertainty against Cleveland.
Philadelphia injuries: Dean Wade questionable (ankle); Tacko Fall, Dominick Barlow and Ariel Hukporti out. Cleveland: Khalifa Diop out; Donovan Mitchell healthy (Predictem). Minor either way.

Cleveland returns Mitchell, Harden (43.5% from three after the deadline trade), Mobley and Allen and adds Peyton Watson (14.6 PPG, 41.1% 3P last season from Denver); Max Strus left for the Clippers (Predictem; SBR). SBR says the Cavs' offense ranked sixth last season with the same core. Helps Cleveland.

[angle] Spacing: neither LeBron nor Brown shot better than 35% from three last season (Predictem), and SBR notes Philly sat 19th of 28 in early offensive rating. That limits Philly's ability to pull away; helps the +3.5.

[spread] Cleveland covered only about 40% of games last season (Predictem) and averaged 114 points over its first seven games last year, five below its season average (WagerTalk). Points against Cleveland, but old ATS data is priced.
Head-to-head: Cleveland went 4-0 SU and 2-1-1 ATS vs Philadelphia last season (WagerTalk); both teams were swept by the Knicks in the playoffs. History is priced; tiebreaker only.

[spread] Projections split: SBR 76ers 118-116 (Cavs +3.5 best bet), Predictem Cavs 116-113 (Cavs +3.5; ESPN model 70.8% Philly to win), WagerTalk 76ers 115-109 (Philly -3.5). Pundit views, not an edge.
Rest: Philadelphia is on one day's rest after a heavy-minutes opener; this is Cleveland's season debut (WagerTalk). Freshness edge to Cleveland, rust risk too.
games.reasoning: I project Philadelphia by about 2.5, a point inside the 3.5. That's under the edge bar, and Jarrett Allen's late status could swing it, so this is a pass. Cleveland is the forced side: the move to 3.5 came with public money after a shaky-shooting opener, Philly's starters logged heavy minutes, and spacing limits its margin. If Allen had been confirmed in and the line had stayed 3.5+, I'd have leaned Cleveland.

research: [spread] Line movement (Predictem, Oct 22): opened OKC -7.5 and climbed to -8.5 even though about two-thirds of spread tickets were on Denver; the writer reads that as bigger money backing OKC. WagerTalk shows the number moving between 7.5 and 9.5 during the week, touching 9.5 on game day and settling at 8.5. The slate's -7.5 is a point better than the market's settled number, on the side the market moved toward (the LESSONS slate-vs-close edge); helps OKC.

[spread] Betting splits (WagerTalk, Oct 22): early on 10/21, 100% of spread money was on Denver; by game day OKC had 63% of money and 56% of tickets. Money flipped to OKC as the line rose. LESSONS: reverse movement toward a favorite has gone 1-4, so it's only weak support.

OKC opened with a 116-104 win over San Antonio on Oct 20 (an earlier game): SGA 32 points, 14-of-31 from three, Wembanyama held to one field goal, Jared McCain hitting bench threes (Predictem/WagerTalk). Form helps OKC.

[angle] OKC traded Lu Dort to Atlanta, and Cason Wallace takes his starting spot (Predictem). OKC still has the league's best defense from last season and forces lots of turnovers. Slight drop in perimeter defense on Murray.

Denver returns its starting five of Jokic, Murray, Gordon, Cam Johnson and Braun at full strength (Predictem/WagerTalk). Its offense ranked top last season and rarely turns the ball over, which blunts OKC's turnover-driven defense (Predictem). Helps Denver.

[angle] Denver's bench is new: Peyton Watson, Tim Hardaway Jr. and Bruce Brown are gone, and DeMar DeRozan, Marvin Bagley III and Alpha Diallo haven't played a regular-season game for Denver. Julian Strawther is out (knee sprain) and Spencer Jones questionable (hamstring) (Predictem/WagerTalk). Thin, untested depth; SBR expects OKC to pull away on depth in the second half. Helps OKC.

[angle] Schedule: this is Denver's season debut, on the road. OKC is on one day's rest after its opener (WagerTalk/Predictem). Denver shot 58.2% and led by 14 after one quarter in its final preseason game vs the Lakers with starters playing. Mixed: OKC has rhythm, Denver has fresh legs.

[spread] Head-to-head last season: OKC went 3-1 SU but 1-3 ATS; the first meeting in OKC went to overtime and another was decided by three; OKC won by 10 in Denver (WagerTalk/Predictem). Those were close games, but history is priced.
Denver was eliminated by Minnesota in last season's playoffs (WagerTalk). Motivation and continuity are neutral.

[spread] Projections split: SBR Thunder 120-110 (OKC -8.5), Predictem Thunder 118-113 (Denver +8.5), WagerTalk Denver 121-118 (Denver +8.5 best bet, Denver ML). These are pundit views, and Denver is the popular contrarian take; not an edge.
A big underdog covers only if it can score with this lineup: Denver's starting five is intact and was the league's top offense, so the dog can score. That argues against laying a big number with OKC.
games.reasoning: The market moved from 7.5 to 8.5, touching 9.5, as money flipped to OKC, and the slate's -7.5 sits a point under where the market settled, the one edge LESSONS says has paid. My projection is OKC by about 9, so the unshaded edge is 1.5 and the shaded edge under 1. That's under the bar, on a favorite, against an intact top offense, so this is a pass with OKC as the forced side. A larger gap between the slate number and the close (e.g. a 9.5 close) would have made it an OKC lean.
